label: QSFP28 50GBASE-FR 2 km
notes: 50GBASE-FR per IEEE 802.3cd-2018 Clause 139, Tables 139-6 (transmit) and 139-7 (receive) - the 2 km rung of the same single-carrier PAM4 family as the LR and ER rows: one 26.5625 GBd carrier at 1311 nm over a 1304.5-1317.5 nm window, duplex LC, RS(544,514) KP4 FEC required. Average launch power -4.1..+3.0 dBm and average receive power -8.1..+3.0 dBm, stressed receiver sensitivity -5.1 dBm OMA. The pair is the published one, not a draft: the D2.1 recirculation ballot moved 50GBASE-FR's launch floor from -3.6 to -4.1 dBm and its receive minimum from -7.6 to -8.1 dBm together (and OMAouter min from -2 to -2.5), so the 4.0 dB a link may spend was unchanged by the move, while the July 2018 ballot carried the stressed figure to -5.1. Two independent transcriptions of the published class print the same pair: Huawei's 50G PAM4 white paper (launch -4.1..3, receive -8.1..3, 7.6 dB power budget, 2 km) and AscentOptics' SFP-50SM31-02C (launch -4.1..3, receive -8.1..3). Read the clause's 7.6 dB power budget carefully: it is the 4 dB channel insertion loss plus a 3.6 dB allowance for the PAM4 eye (TDECQ), and because the engine compares average launch with average receive, -4.1 - (-8.1) = 4.0 is the whole figure a link may spend - the same arithmetic as the LR, 25GBASE-LR and 100GBASE-LR1 rows, and the reason this rung is 2 km and not 10. Consequence at the default 3 dB margin, measured by driving budget.pointToPoint: 2 km bare is 0.7 dB of fibre and reads marginal at 3.3 dB of headroom; one patch panel at each end (0.6 dB) makes it 1.3 dB and reads fail on 2.7 dB of headroom, naming sensitivity -8.1 dBm. `ok` needs margin + 2 = 5 dB of headroom and the class offers 4.0 at zero loss, so no 50GBASE-FR link reads ok at the default margin; a bare 2 km span reads ok only with marginDb 1 (measured). Treat this as a short-reach rung budgeted with a deliberately lower margin, or take a better-than-class receive figure from the module's own test report. Overload is not the problem here: the launch ceiling +3.0 dBm equals the receiver maximum +3.0 dBm, so a back-to-back pair sits exactly on the overload point and the engine asks for no pad (it refuses only a span that lands strictly above it), and one mating takes it 0.3 dB clear - the opposite of 50GBASE-ER, whose +0.4 dBm floor is already 3.8 dB above its -3.4 dBm receive maximum. Reach is a separate verdict and binds before the budget: 2100 m is refused by name even though 0.735 dB of fibre still leaves the headroom intact, because the route is longer than the 2 km the class supports. The row says 1310 nm - the window the cables publish attenuation for, as the LR row does - although the carrier sits at 1311 nm. One carrier, so budget.pointToPoint refuses this row against a 25G or 100G optic on speed, which the four-lane rows cannot give. Class figures from the clause and its transcriptions, not one measured module: replace the row with the module actually purchased before pricing a build.
